title: Future-Proof Coding Agents – Bill Chen & Brian Fioca, OpenAI
talk_summary: OpenAI engineers describe coding agents as UI + model + harness, and argue harness quality depends on matching prompts/tools to each model's trained habits. They present Codex as an off-the-shelf harness/SDK with compaction, sandboxing, MCP, and CI/PR integrations that other products can wrap or call.

takeaways.what_they_do: They align prompts/tools to each model's trained habits, avoid overprompting, and ask the model what instruction caused slow behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you let the model just do the behaviors that it's used to and don't overprompt it, it'll actually perform really better.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat compaction as a harness responsibility: decide when to trigger it, what state to reinject, and how to preserve cache efficiency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When do you trigger compaction? When do you reinject? How do you worry about uh cache optimization during that

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the harness should absorb model-specific prompt/tool differences so product code does not need re-tuning for every model upgrade.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you no longer have to care about prioritize optimizing the prompt and tools with every model upgrade.

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose Codex as an SDK/CLI that can be called programmatically and nested inside another agent for coding tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Codeex is an SDK. It can be called through a TypeScript library. You can call it programmatically

takeaways.what_they_do: They point to a GitHub action that invokes a coding agent to resolve merge conflicts on PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's a GitHub action that you can plug into to have it merge merge conflicts on PRs

takeaways.what_they_do: They list sandboxing, prompt forwarding, permissions, and port management as core harness plumbing that must be handled explicitly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: security considerations you have with sandboxing, prompt forwarding, permissions, uh, port management.
